title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
why_read: A careful ablation study isolating what actually matters in tokenizer design (search procedure vs. optimization objective) gives concrete, actionable guidance for building better LLM tokenizers.
analysis: This paper disentangles two confounded design choices in text tokenization for language models: the optimization objective (compression vs likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up vs top-down), by building two new hybrid tokenizers to fill out the full 2x2 combination. Testing across model sizes and languages, they find that the search procedure, not the objective, is what drives compression performance measured in bits-per-byte, though this doesn't predict grammatical performance on the BLiMP benchmark. This is a rigorous piece of applied research that clarifies a widely-used but poorly understood component of LLM pipelines, useful for anyone building or tuning tokenizers.
